page.layout: One page of running text, with a woodcut ornament beside the start of the chapter. Two marginal notes stand in the right margin. Running head at top, page number at top right.

main_text.p: bet esse alimetum,ut concoqui possit. Con-coquitur autem a calore,qui concoquendi vim habet. Quare in animatis omnibus naturis calor infit necesse est. Sunt & aliae nutrientis animae vires, quibus quaelibet tum animantis,tum stirpis pars praedita est. Earum una est alimentum attrahendi:secunda ipsum retinendi:tertia concoquendi:postrema expellendi quod excrementum est. Quoniam autem a fine om[?]es res denominantur,finisque animae propositus est aliquid simile ei procreare,quod eam habet,haud dubie prima vis & principium generandi huiusmodi simile ipsa anima est.
main_text.head: CAP. IX. De vi fentiendi.
main_text.p: RIMUM autem de omni fenfu comuniter, deinde speciatim de vnoquoque disputandum est.C.5.l. Senfus quidem tum fit, cum corpus aliquod afficitur,quoniam quaedam alteratio est.2.de anima. Quemadmodum autem duobus modis aliquid sentire dicitur,actu nimirum, & potentia:ita duobus modis sensus dicitur. unus enim sentiendi vis est:alter ipse actus & sentiendi operatio. Eodemque modo sentire actu dicitur,quo contemplari & intelligere actu. Sed hoc interest,quod ea, quae sensum mouent,extra sensum sunt,propterea quod rerum singularium & externarum sensus sit:sed quae intelligutur in ipso intellectu

page.notes: The woodcut initial R of "RIMUM" is read as "RIMUM" with the first letter joined to "autem" in the printed initial. The word "omnes" in the first paragraph is partly obscured by a mark and is read as "om[?]es". "intelligutur" is doubtful. The second note in the right margin is printed as "2.de a-" and "nima.", so it is joined here as "2.de anima.". The printed "Sen-fus" has no hyphen at the line end, so it is written whole. The final line of the page ends mid-sentence and continues on the next page.
